subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session hook-agent deliveries be rejected with 409, queued or serialized, or remain parallel by default, and should that policy be opt-in per direct hook and mapping?
rationale: The choice changes public HTTP retry semantics, session-state behavior, and security-sensitive hook routing, so automation should not choose it from source inspection alone.

options.title: Add an explicit overlap policy
options.body: Preserve current parallel async behavior by default and add a configured per-hook policy such as reject, queue, or parallel for trusted integrations.

options.title: Fold this into queued webhooks
options.body: Make the broader queued webhook design own burst handling, backlog visibility, and concurrency controls before closing this narrower request.

options.title: Make same-session overlap fail closed
options.body: Return 409 for overlapping deliveries by default and accept the compatibility cost for existing asynchronous webhook callers.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit overlap policy
recommendation.body: Preserve current parallel async behavior by default and add a configured per-hook policy such as reject, queue, or parallel for trusted integrations.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a Gateway session/security policy decision rather than only a local hook dispatch implementation detail.
